ABSTRACT

DISTINGUISHING METHANE LEAKS FROM OPERATING TRANSIENTS IN GAS PROCESSING FACILITIES: A CRITICAL REVIEW OF PHYSICS BASED, DATADRIVEN, AND HYBRID DIAGNOSTIC METHODS

Journal: Journal CleanWAS (JCleanWAS)
Author: Justine Bundi, Joan Nyika, Ednah Onyari
This is an open access article distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution License CC BY 4.0, which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original work is properly cited

Doi: 10.26480/jcleanwas.02.26.75.85

Fugitive methane emissions from gas plants are a potent and needless source of emissions which must be monitored to address them. However, monitoring devices need to differentiate the leak signal from the overwhelming number of transients, every one of which is the deviation from the plant which almost never operates steadily as a result of start-ups, shutdowns, composition variations, compressor recycling, venting, flaring and loading. Each false alarm wastes the operator’s time and reduces their confidence, hence deferring the action on the actual emissions. This literature review applies the signal detection framework involving leak and transient hypotheses, observation vector and asymmetric costs to assess three categories of methods. Physics-based methods (optical gas imaging, laser absorption, acoustic sensing, Method 21 surveys and balance reconciliation) are transparent and standardizable yet driven by thresholds such that the behavior of false alarms gets worse with the changing conditions of operations. Data-driven methods (multivariate statistical process control, anomaly detection and supervised classification) have the capability to learn the norm from the historian database yet constrained by lack of labeled data and distribution change. Hybrid architectures combining the physics-based residuals and the learned state-dependent criterion for their assessment, robust alarm design and human confirmation represent the only viable approach to low false-alarm leak detection by architectural arguments, a claim which is considered unproven here. The singleblind validation proves that the actual performance varies substantially across different methods and operating conditions. This paper provides a comparative assessment, false-alarm taxonomy, deployment
guidance and research agenda.
